about: Skill tracks: each groups the framework techniques one area of practice is about, says where to practise it in the estate, and names certifications whose PUBLISHED syllabus covers the same skill area. This is not exam content and makes no claim about any exam; check each provider's current syllabus. Exam rules forbid sharing exam material, and the range never contains any.

tracks.title: Identity and Active Directory
tracks.why: Most intrusions run through accounts: guessed or reused passwords, ticket abuse, and changes to groups and policies.
practise: Range tasks: Defending the workstations, Stopping repeat attacks
The Active Directory lab: ./securax range (GOAD), in a lab you own
Purple-team view: run an attack in the lab, then find it in the logs
certifications: OffSec OSCP+ (includes an Active Directory set)

tracks.title: Linux hosts and services
tracks.why: Servers are kept by persistence that hides in keys, scheduled jobs, new accounts and web shells.
practise: The lite range: every gamebox host, through the jump box

tracks.title: Network edge and public services
tracks.why: Public services are scanned within minutes of going online; defence is filtering, watching and keeping only what must be public.
practise: Range task: Defending the network edge
Target checks: keep every public service green while you filter

tracks.title: Data theft and ransomware
tracks.why: The impact that ends careers: data leaving, and systems encrypted for ransom.
practise: Range tasks: Protecting the files, Analyse the dropped program

tracks.title: AI and LLM systems (frontier AI threats)
tracks.why: AI assistants that read documents and use tools can be steered by hidden instructions, leak data and act without a person approving.
practise: Range task: Defending the staff AI assistant
The estate's own AI red team and purple loop: ./securax purple (doc 30)
The AI gateway's guardrails and audit trail (apps/llm-gateway)
certifications: No mainstream certification yet; study the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications and NIST AI 600-1 (the estate maps both)

tracks.title: Reporting under pressure
tracks.why: Exercises and real incidents are judged on clear, timely, evidenced reports as much as on technical work.
practise: Incident and situation reports in every exercise; the judges' feedback
certifications: HTB CPTS and OffSec OSCP+ both require a professional report
